newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico denies reports of new rebel clash.
newsitem.headline: Mexico denies reports of new rebel clash.

text.p: The Mexican government denied on Friday a newspaper report that 20 people may have died in a clash between guerrillas and the army in the mountains of eastern Veracruz state.

La Jornada newspaper on Thursday quoted local media as saying that rebels, probably from the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), had fought troops in the mountains near the town of Zongolica, 140 miles (220 km) east of Mexico City.

The EPR is Mexico's newest guerrilla group. Since its surprise first appearance on June 28, rebels have attacked in at least four states and killed more than a dozen troops and police as part of a Marxist campaign calling for the overthrow of President Ernesto Zedillo.

Government chief spokesman Dionisio Perez Jacome flatly denied the reports of a battle in Veracruz state. "This is totally false," he told Reuters. "There was no clash, there is not a single person wounded. I deny this totally."
Veracruz state officials also denied a report carried on Thursday by a state television station, Veravision del Oriente, saying 20 people had died in combat in the area.

La Jornada said the mayor of a small town in the area had spoken of the dead to a local newspaper. The mayor of San Miguel Eloxochitlan, Gilberto Oguama Campa, told Veracruz's La tarde de Zongolica newspaper fighting had erupted on Thursday afternoon.

But a city official in Zongolica, who did not wish to be identified, told Reuters there had been no fighting in that municipality. A local church worker in Zongolica told Reuters some 40 truckloads of heavily armed police have fanned out throught the area, apparently hunting EPR members, but she said she was unaware of reports of fighting.
Mexican newspapers on Friday also carried a statement by the EPR that denied responsibility for a recent wave of bomb threats in the Pacific coastal resort of Acapulco.
